correctness.rationale: The logit coboundary forces x0+x1=2m and the established scalar equation, with a complete converse. Two-step Jacobian multiplication yields exact trace T and determinant D. Strict convexity of 1/[x(1-x)] proves 1-T+D>0 for every nonconstant two-cycle. Schur inequalities and the two limiting equilibrium eigenvalues prove the sharp cp1=1/3 near-birth split away from equality; the critical equality is not classified.

historical_scientific_assessment.correctness: The earlier proof of the logit reduction, scalar H_m monotonicity and Schur identity was mathematically valid, and its exact rational witness was checked. Finite samples corroborated but did not prove the universal result.
historical_scientific_assessment.mathematical_value: The original structural no-cycle regime and exact threshold are useful as consequences of the scalar reduction, but the independently valuable remainder is the two-dimensional transverse Floquet obstruction and sharp stability division.
historical_scientific_assessment.originality_comparison: The earlier comparison credited Chotibut et al. for the symmetric scalar case and Metaxas–Sapsis for the model and stationary mean, but missed the all-target scalar two-cycle theorem of Kryzhevich–Zhang–Chmara (2024), Lemma 3.1, citing an even earlier general-target result. Its claim of a novel all-parameter scalar count is not retained.

originality.rationale: The general-target scalar two-cycle uniqueness, existence threshold and amplitude are prior results by Kryzhevich–Zhang–Chmara and sources; these are not counted as novel. The surviving mathematical claim is the exact two-dimensional Floquet +1 exclusion and transverse near-birth stability split, not implied by scalar counts or previously inspected same-map inverse-fiber results. The model originators supply the underlying equations and numerical bifurcation regimes; priority remains qualified.

scientific_scope: Transverse Floquet stability and global +1 exclusion for interior two-cycles at k=1; scalar orbit census credited to prior one-dimensional theory

value.rationale: The sharp cp1=1/3 threshold shows precisely when the added lagged risk-belief dimension changes a newborn scalar-flip cycle from attracting to nonattracting, while the global +1 exclusion constrains its later bifurcation mechanism. Both concern a natural dynamical system and are not mere scalar threshold substitutions.
